Main article: [Yang Yuanqing](/wiki/Yang_Yuanqing "Yang Yuanqing")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Yang_Yuanqing.jpeg/250px-Yang_Yuanqing.jpeg)](/wiki/File:Yang_Yuanqing.jpeg)

[Yang Yuanqing](/wiki/Yang_Yuanqing "Yang Yuanqing"), Lenovo's Chairman and CEO

Yang Yuanqing is the chairman and chief executive officer of Lenovo. One of his major achievements was leading Lenovo to become the best-selling personal computer brand in China since 1997. In 2001, *[Bloomberg Businessweek](/wiki/Bloomberg_Businessweek "Bloomberg Businessweek")* named him one of Asia's rising stars in business.[[195]](#cite_note-195) Yang was president and CEO of Lenovo until 2004, when Lenovo closed its acquisition of IBM's PC division, after which Yang was succeeded as Lenovo CEO by IBM's [Stephen M. Ward Jr.](/wiki/Steve_Ward_(businessman) "Steve Ward (businessman)") Ward was succeeded by [William Amelio](/wiki/William_Amelio "William Amelio") on 20 December 2005. In February 2009, Yang replaced Amelio as CEO and has served in that capacity ever since. Yang was chairman of Lenovo's board from 2004 to 2008, and returned as chairman in 2012 alongside his role as CEO.

In 2012, Yang received a $3 million bonus as a reward for record profits, which he in turn redistributed to about 10,000 of Lenovo's employees. According to Lenovo spokesman, Jeffrey Shafer, Yang felt that it would be the right thing to, "redirect [the money] to the employees as a real tangible gesture for what they done." Shafer also said that Yang, who owns about eight per cent of Lenovo's stock, "felt that he was rewarded well simply as the owner of the company".[[196]](#cite_note-Bonus-196) The bonuses were mostly distributed among staff working in positions such as production and reception who received an average of CN¥2,000 or about US$314. fanoutqa_015855.t: The Bronx :: Demographics :: Race, ethnicity, language, and immigration :: 2010 census :: chunk_0024
fanoutqa_015855.x:
The Bronx :: Demographics :: Race, ethnicity, language, and immigration :: 2010 census :: chunk_0024
According to the 2010 Census, 53.5% of Bronx's population was of Hispanic, Latino, or Spanish origin (they may be of any race); 30.1% non-Hispanic Black or African American, 10.9% of the population was non-Hispanic White, 3.4% non-Hispanic Asian, 1.2% of two or more races (non-Hispanic), and 0.6% from some other race (non-Hispanic).

As of 2010, 46.29% (584,463) of Bronx residents aged five and older spoke [Spanish](/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language") at home, while 44.02% (555,767) spoke [English](/wiki/English_language "English language"), 2.48% (31,361) [African languages](/wiki/Languages_of_Africa "Languages of Africa"), 0.91% (11,455) [French](/wiki/French_language "French language"), 0.90% (11,355) [Italian](/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language"), 0.87% (10,946) [various Indic languages](/wiki/Indo-Aryan_languages "Indo-Aryan languages"), 0.70% (8,836) [other Indo-European languages](/wiki/Indo-European_languages "Indo-European languages"), and [Chinese](/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language") was spoken at home by 0.50% (6,610) of the population over the age of five. In total, 55.98% (706,783) of the Bronx's population age five and older spoke a language at home other than English.[[141]](#cite_note-141) A [Garifuna](/wiki/Garifuna_language "Garifuna language")-speaking community from [Honduras](/wiki/Honduras "Honduras") and [Guatemala](/wiki/Guatemala "Guatemala") also makes the Bronx its home.[[142]](#cite_note-142)

fanoutqa_025071.t: OPEC :: Market information :: Publications and research :: chunk_0025
fanoutqa_025071.x:
OPEC :: Market information :: Publications and research :: chunk_0025
[![refer to caption](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Jodi-circle-logo.png/250px-Jodi-circle-logo.png)](/wiki/File:Jodi-circle-logo.png)

The logo of [JODI](/wiki/Joint_Organisations_Data_Initiative "Joint Organisations Data Initiative"), in which OPEC is a founding member

In April 2001, OPEC collaborated with five other international organizations ([APEC](/wiki/Asia-Pacific_Economic_Cooperation "Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation"), [Eurostat](/wiki/Eurostat "Eurostat"), [IEA](/wiki/International_Energy_Agency "International Energy Agency"), [OLADE](/w/index.php?title=Latin_American_Energy_Organisation&action=edit&redlink=1 "Latin American Energy Organisation (page does not exist)"), [UNSD](/wiki/United_Nations_Statistics_Division "United Nations Statistics Division")) to improve the availability and reliability of oil data. They launched the Joint Oil Data Exercise, which in 2005 was joined by [IEF](/wiki/International_Energy_Forum "International Energy Forum") and renamed the [Joint Organisations Data Initiative](/wiki/Joint_Organisations_Data_Initiative "Joint Organisations Data Initiative") (JODI), covering more than 90% of the global oil market. [GECF](/wiki/Gas_Exporting_Countries_Forum "Gas Exporting Countries Forum") joined as an eighth partner in 2014, enabling JODI also to cover nearly 90% of the global market for natural gas.[[222]](#cite_note-225)

Since 2007, OPEC has published the "World Oil Outlook" (WOO) annually, in which it presents a comprehensive analysis of the global oil industry including medium- and long-term projections for supply and demand.[[223]](#cite_note-226) OPEC also produces an "Annual Statistical Bulletin" (ASB),[[106]](#cite_note-ASB-106) and publishes more-frequent updates in its "Monthly Oil Market Report" (MOMR)[[224]](#cite_note-227) and "OPEC Bulletin".[[225]](#cite_note-228)

**Washington, D.C.**, officially the **District of Columbia** and commonly known as simply **Washington** or **D.C.**, is the [capital city](/wiki/Capital_city "Capital city") and [federal district](/wiki/Federal_district_of_the_United_States "Federal district of the United States")[[a]](#cite_note-11) of the [United States](/wiki/United_States "United States"). The city is on the [Potomac River](/wiki/Potomac_River "Potomac River") across from [Virginia](/wiki/Virginia "Virginia") and shares land borders with [Maryland](/wiki/Maryland "Maryland") to its north and east. It was named after [George Washington](/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington"), a [Founding Father](/wiki/Founding_Fathers_of_the_United_States "Founding Fathers of the United States") and the first [president of the United States](/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States"). The district is named for [Columbia](/wiki/Columbia_(personification) "Columbia (personification)"), the female [personification of the nation](/wiki/National_personification "National personification"), through which human form and attributes are applied to the United States.

The [U.S. Constitution](/wiki/Constitution_of_the_United_States "Constitution of the United States") in 1789 called for the creation of a [federal district](/wiki/Federal_district "Federal district") under [exclusive jurisdiction](/wiki/District_of_Columbia_home_rule "District of Columbia home rule") of the [U.S. Congress](/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress"). As such, Washington, D.C., is not part of any [state](/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state"), and is not one itself. The [Residence Act](/wiki/Residence_Act "Residence Act"), adopted on July 16, 1790, approved the creation of the [capital district](/wiki/Capital_districts_and_territories "Capital districts and territories") along the Potomac River, and is considered the city's founding date. Five Patriots head coaches, Holovak, [Chuck Fairbanks](/wiki/Chuck_Fairbanks "Chuck Fairbanks"), Berry, Parcells, and Belichick, have been named [Coach of the Year](/wiki/AP_NFL_Coach_of_the_Year_award "AP NFL Coach of the Year award") by at least one major news organization. **Amin Hassan Nasser** ([Arabic](/wiki/Arabic_language "Arabic language"): أمين حسن الناصر) is the President and [CEO](/wiki/Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer") of [Saudi Aramco](/wiki/Saudi_Aramco "Saudi Aramco"), the world's largest oil producer. He became acting president and chief executive in May 2015 before assuming the position permanently in September 2015.[[1]](#cite_note-:1-1) During his tenure at Aramco, he has criticized [fossil fuel divestment](/wiki/Fossil_fuel_divestment "Fossil fuel divestment") and promoted expansion and investment into oil production.[[2]](#cite_note-:2-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3)

Nasser holds a [bachelor's degree](/wiki/Bachelor%27s_degree "Bachelor's degree") in [petroleum engineering](/wiki/Petroleum_engineering "Petroleum engineering") from the [King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals in Dhahran](/wiki/King_Fahd_University_of_Petroleum_and_Minerals "King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals"). He completed the Saudi Aramco Management Development Seminar in Washington, D.C., in 1999; the Saudi Aramco Global Business Program in 2000; and the Senior Executive Program at [Columbia University](/wiki/Columbia_University "Columbia University") in 2002.[[4]](#cite_note-4)

The [United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland](/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Northern_Ireland "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland"), referred to as simply "Great Britain", has been represented at every modern [Olympic Games](/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games"). As of the [2024 Summer Olympics](/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics"), it is third in the [all-time Summer Olympic medal table](/wiki/All-time_Olympic_Games_medal_table "All-time Olympic Games medal table") by overall number of medals, and fourth in number of gold medals won. London hosted the [Summer Olympic Games](/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games "Summer Olympic Games") in [1908](/wiki/1908_Summer_Olympics "1908 Summer Olympics"), [1948](/wiki/1948_Summer_Olympics "1948 Summer Olympics") and [2012](/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics").

Athletes from the United Kingdom compete as part of the Great Britain and Northern Ireland Olympic Team,[[1]](#cite_note-1) branded "[Team GB](/wiki/Team_GB "Team GB")". The team is organised by the [British Olympic Association](/wiki/British_Olympic_Association "British Olympic Association"), the [National Olympic Committee](/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee "National Olympic Committee") for the UK. Team GB also represents the United Kingdom's [Overseas Territories](/wiki/British_Overseas_Territories "British Overseas Territories") (with the exceptions of [Bermuda](/wiki/Bermuda_at_the_Olympics "Bermuda at the Olympics"), the [British Virgin Islands](/wiki/British_Virgin_Islands_at_the_Olympics "British Virgin Islands at the Olympics"), and the [Cayman Islands](/wiki/Cayman_Islands_at_the_Olympics "Cayman Islands at the Olympics")), and the three [Crown Dependencies](/wiki/Crown_Dependencies "Crown Dependencies") of [Guernsey](/wiki/Guernsey "Guernsey"), [Jersey](/wiki/Jersey "Jersey"), and the [Isle of Man](/wiki/Isle_of_Man "Isle of Man"). The **president of** **the People's Republic of China**, is the [state representative](/wiki/List_of_state_representatives_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China "List of state representatives of the People's Republic of China") of the [People's Republic of China](/wiki/People%27s_Republic_of_China "People's Republic of China"). On its own, it is a [ceremonial office](/wiki/Figurehead "Figurehead") and has no real power in China's [political system](/wiki/Politics_of_China "Politics of China"), though since 1993, the post has been concurrently held by the [general secretary](/wiki/General_Secretary_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party "General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party") of the [Chinese Communist Party](/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party") (CCP) and [chairman of the Central Military Commission](/wiki/Chairman_of_the_Central_Military_Commission_(China) "Chairman of the Central Military Commission (China)"), who is the country's [top leader](/wiki/Paramount_leader "Paramount leader"). While the office has many of the characteristics of a [head of state](/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state"), the [country's constitution](/wiki/Constitution_of_China "Constitution of China") does not define it as such.

The presidency in its current form was the chairman of the Central People's Government of the People's Republic of China, which was established on 1 October 1949 by a decision of the [Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference](/wiki/Chinese_People%27s_Political_Consultative_Conference "Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference"). It was replaced in the [1954 constitution](/wiki/1954_Constitution_of_China "1954 Constitution of China") with the office of state chairman. It was successively held by [Mao Zedong](/wiki/Mao_Zedong "Mao Zedong") and [Liu Shaoqi](/wiki/Liu_Shaoqi "Liu Shaoqi").
